newsitem.title: CANADA: Finning aims to close U.K. acquisition soon.
newsitem.headline: Finning aims to close U.K. acquisition soon.

text.p: Finning Ltd, the world's biggest dealer of Caterpillar Inc equipment, said on Wednesday it hoped to close a British acquisition early next year that would add about C$500 million to annual revenues.

Finning said in August that it was in talks with Unilever Plc to buy its H Leverton Ltd unit, which holds the Caterpillar franchise for parts of England not handled by Finning. Investors have been awaiting progress on the deal.
"It's our hope we will have the closing in the first quarter," Finning president Jim Shepard said in an interview.

While some investors were impatient for the deal to close, Shepard said the transaction was complicated because it hinged partly on a parallel move by Unilever to sell separately Leverton's business in six African countries.
Shepard declined to discuss specifics of the talks other than Leverton's impact on revenues, citing a confidentiality agreement with Unilever on the negotiations.
But he said the acquisition would have a positive impact on Finning's earnings. "It will not be dilutive. It will be a positive (change) to our earnings," he said.
Finning, which has operations in western Canada, Chile and Britain, had revenues of C$1.7 billion in 1995.
Under the proposed deal, Finning would sell its dealership in Poland and its U.K. finance portfolio. Proceeds from those deals along with debt would finance the Leverton acquisition.
"In other words, at the moment we aren't contemplating an equity issue," Shepard said.
The loss of the Polish operation would have little impact on Finning because it had been running at break-even, he said.
Goepel Shields analyst Carl Hoyt praised the Leverton deal as offering prime near-term growth prospects for Finning. "It's going to be a tremendous opportunity," he said.

He estimated in a recent report that Finning would pay about C$200 million for Leverton. Analysts projected the deal would initially add about C$0.50 a share to Finning annual earnings and about a further C$0.10 a share when the operations were fully integrated over the next two to three years.

Finning earned C$77.5 million or C$2.00 a share last year and C$67.7 million or C$1.74 a share in the first nine months of 1996 including a C$7 million or C$0.18 a share gain on the sale of real estate.
Shepard declined to comment on earnings forecasts. Consensus estimates projected Finning would earn C$2.15 a share this year including the gain and C$2.30 to C$2.35 next year.
But he anticipated strong profit and revenue growth in Chile where demand for heavy equipment was fueled by expansion in mining and infrastructure projects.
In western Canada and Britain, 1997 looked to be relatively flat for the company, he said.
Finning shares have staged a strong rise in recent weeks, jumping from around 23.90 on October 10 to 28.80 on November 29 before retreating to about 28.

The move coincided with company presentations to institutions in the United States and Canada. Shepard said investors responded well to the company's performance, which included 63 years of uninterrupted profit growth.
"That's a record that is pretty hard to match," he said.

Finning has sought since 1980 to diversify from its traditional base serving the British Columbia forestry industry. After the Leverton acquisition, it expected 60 percent of its revenues to be generated outside Canada.
